title: Spotify
summary: Music streaming: audio files encoded at several bitrates and served in chunks from CDNs, metadata and playlists from sharded services, offline downloads, and an event pipeline that feeds royalties and recommendations.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Search and play tracks; playlists; library; offline downloads
Playback starts < 300 ms; no stutter on flaky mobile networks

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Five terabits a second of audio has to come from CDNs; our own servers handle metadata, auth and the event pipeline.

GET  /v1/tracks/{id}                -> metadata + available formats
GET  /v1/tracks/{id}/stream?quality -> signed CDN URLs for file chunks (+ decryption key)
GET  /v1/me/playlists  /  PUT /v1/playlists/{id}/tracks
POST /v1/events  [ {type: play_started|progress|play_ended, trackId, ms, ts} ]  (batched)

head: Data
Key
Store
rows: Sharded store with version history (collaborative edits)

blocks.caption: Bytes from the CDN, everything else from services

items: Play → playback service checks entitlement, returns signed CDN URLs and a decryption key.
Client fetches the first chunk at low bitrate for fast start, then adapts up.
Client prefetches the next track near the end of the current one.
Playback events batch to the event pipeline (play counts after 30 s of listening).

sections.title: Deep dive: fast start and smooth playback

items: Encode each track at multiple bitrates; split into chunks so the client can switch quality mid-track.
Start with a small low-bitrate chunk, raise quality as the buffer fills (adaptive bitrate).
Local cache on device holds recently played tracks; offline downloads store encrypted files with a license that must be refreshed (e.g. every 30 days).
Long tail: popular tracks are hot in every CDN; rare tracks are fetched from origin/shield on demand.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Most plays are popular tracks that the CDN already has, and the next track is prefetched, so the perceived start time is usually zero.

sections.title: Deep dive: play events, royalties and recommendations

items: Billions of events/day; clients batch and retry, so ingestion must dedupe by event ID.
Royalties need exactly-once counting → idempotent aggregation keyed by (user, track, play session).
Recommendations: collaborative filtering on listening matrices + audio/NLP embeddings; batch jobs build weekly playlists, online models rank home shelves.
Events delivered at-least-once to a durable pipeline, then processed in batch and streaming jobs.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Durable buffering; counts are not user-facing in real time
Revision-based merges (ops), like a mini Google Docs

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: ABR + prefetch, offline licensing, royalty counting.

items.title: Wrap-up
items.text: Multi-CDN, release pre-warm, metrics: start time, rebuffer rate.

items.a: Inverted index over tracks/artists/albums with typo tolerance and popularity boosting; typeahead cached per prefix.

items.q: How would you build a 'what's playing with friends' feature?
items.a: Publish play events to a social fan-out service; WebSocket or polling for friends' activity.
Encryption with DRM keys per track, signed short-lived URLs, license checks for offline.

items: Bytes from CDN; services for metadata and keys.
